2027-03-17.title: Sixth Wednesday of the Great Fast
2027-03-17.readTitle: Readings of the day (First Set; mapped from the official calendar, verify locally)
readings: Whoever loves a brother or sister lives in the light
Where two or three are gathered
2027-03-17.alt: Season of the Great Fast (Sauma Ramba). In the Latin calendar today is the memorial of St Patrick.
2027-03-17.verse: For where two or three are gathered in my name, I am there among them.
theo: John writes as an old man to children in the faith, and he says something that sounds like a riddle: “Beloved, I am writing you no new commandment, but an old commandment that you have had from the beginning.” And then, almost at once: “Yet I am writing you a new commandment.” The commandment of love is old, because it was given at the beginning and is written in every human heart. It is new, because in Christ it has been lived to the end, “because the darkness is passing away and the true light is already shining.” Then John draws a line no one can argue with: “Whoever says, ‘I am in the light,’ while hating a brother or sister, is still in the darkness. Whoever loves a brother or sister lives in the light, and in such a person there is no cause for stumbling.” Hatred blinds: “whoever hates another believer is in the darkness, walks in the darkness, and does not know the way to go, because the darkness has brought on blindness.” Many Kerala families carry old quarrels, over a boundary wall, a share of family property, a wedding where someone was not honoured. They can last for generations, and people still come to the same church on Sunday and sit apart. John's word is plain: no amount of fasting puts us in the light while such a quarrel is kept alive by our own choice.

The Gospel gives the way out, step by step. “If another member of the church sins against you, go and point out the fault when the two of you are alone.” Not gossip first, not a public scene, but a quiet word face to face. “If the member listens to you, you have regained that one.” The goal is not to win an argument but to win back a brother or sister. Only if that fails do others become involved, and then the Church; and the Church receives the power to bind and to loose, which the Lord exercises above all in the sacrament of reconciliation. Then Jesus speaks of prayer: “if two of you agree on earth about anything you ask, it will be done for you by my Father in heaven. For where two or three are gathered in my name, I am there among them.” Notice the order: first reconciliation, then agreement in prayer, then his presence. Two people who were not speaking, and who come together again in his name, become a place where Christ stands. The Latin Church today remembers St Patrick, who returned as a missionary to the land where he had been a slave, and made of his former captors a people gathered in Christ's name.
outline: Ask: is there someone I have not spoken to in years?
Point 1 · An old commandment, a new commandment
Love, as old as creation and as new as the Cross.
Point 2 · Go and point out the fault
Point 3 · Two or three in my name
Reconciled, agreed, and Christ among us.
“Where two or three are gathered in my name, I am there among them.”
live: Before Pesaha, speak privately and gently to one person with whom you have an unresolved quarrel.
Agree with one family member on a single intention, and pray for it together every night until Easter.
2027-03-17.prayer: Lord Jesus Christ, true light already shining, drive the darkness of hatred from our hearts. Give us courage to go to those who have wronged us, not to win, but to win them back. Gather us in your name, so that we may agree in prayer and know that you are among us. Amen.
altar: Before the anaphora of the Holy Qurbana we exchange the sign of peace, because no one can bring a gift to the altar while refusing peace to a brother or sister; then Christ is truly present among those gathered in his name.

quick: The commandment of love is old as creation and new in Christ.
Whoever hates a brother or sister walks in darkness and is blind.
Go privately to the one who has wronged you; aim to win them back.
2027-03-17.action: Speak gently to one person you have been avoiding.
2027-03-17.question: Whom have I lost because I never went to speak to them alone?

family.explain: Jesus said: if someone hurts you, go and talk to them quietly, just the two of you, and try to make peace. He also said: when two or three people pray together in my name, I am right there with them. So when our family prays together, Jesus is with us!
family.intention: We pray for families and neighbours who are not speaking to each other.
family.ask: Ask: “Is there anyone we need to make peace with before Easter?”

illus: Two brothers in a village near Pala had not spoken for eleven years after dividing their father's land. Their houses stood forty metres apart. During the Lenten retreat the preacher read Matthew 18 and asked everyone to look at the person they would least like to sit beside. The younger brother saw the older one three rows ahead. That night he walked the forty metres with a packet of sugar, the way their mother used to send things between the houses. The older brother opened the door, looked at the sugar, and said only, “Come in, the tea is ready.”

pm.open: Lord Jesus, you promised to be among those gathered in your name. We are gathered; be among us now. Amen.
share: Whoever loves a brother or sister lives in the light (1 John 2:10). Where does a hidden resentment keep me in the dark?
Go and point out the fault when the two of you are alone (Matthew 18:15). Do I speak to people, or about them?
Where two or three are gathered in my name, I am there among them (Matthew 18:20). How can our group be a place where Christ is found?
pm.resp: Lord, make us one in your name.
interc: For the Church, that she may be a house of reconciliation.
For families divided by property and old quarrels.
For priests who hear confessions in these last days of the fast.
For the people of Ireland, through the prayers of St Patrick.
For our group, that we may agree in prayer and live in the light.
pm.close: Father, your Son promised to be among those gathered in his name. Heal our divisions, open our mouths to speak peace, and keep us in the light of love. Through Christ our Lord. Amen.

homily: Dear friends, John says that the commandment of love is old, given from the beginning, and also new, because in Christ the darkness is passing away and the true light is already shining (1 John 2:8).

He is blunt: whoever says he is in the light while hating a brother or sister is still in the darkness (1 John 2:9). We can fast, pray and come to church every day, and still walk in darkness if we keep a quarrel alive.

Jesus shows the way: if someone sins against you, go and speak to them alone. If they listen, you have regained that one (Matthew 18:15). The aim is not to win an argument but to win back a brother or sister.
Then he promises: where two or three are gathered in my name, I am there among them (Matthew 18:20). Before Pesaha, let us take the first step toward someone we have been avoiding. Amen.
kids: Children, Jesus said that when two or three people pray together in his name, he is right there with them. If you have quarrelled with a brother, sister or friend, make peace today, and then pray together. Jesus will be with you!

intro: Theme: “For where two or three are gathered in my name, I am there among them.”
The old and new commandment of love, the Lord's way of reconciliation, and his presence among those gathered in his name.

q: For with you is the fountain of life; in your light we see light.
Whoever loves a brother or sister lives in the light, and in such a person there is no cause for stumbling.
points.apply: Examine your heart for any resentment you have chosen to keep, and offer it to God today.

q: You shall not hate in your heart anyone of your kin; you shall reprove your neighbor, or you will incur guilt yourself.
If another member of the church sins against you, go and point out the fault when the two of you are alone. If the member listens to you, you have regained that one.
points.apply: Go privately and gently to one person with whom you have an unresolved quarrel.

points.h: Two or three in my name
q: How very good and pleasant it is when kindred live together in unity!
For where two or three are gathered in my name, I am there among them.
points.apply: Agree with a family member on one intention and pray for it together each night until Easter.

concl: Love is the old commandment made new in Christ; hatred keeps us in darkness however much we fast.
Go to your brother or sister, win them back, and pray together: Christ will be among you.
2027-03-17.resolve: Before Pesaha, take one step of reconciliation and begin one shared prayer.
